Dear Dr. Henderson,

Thank you for evaluating Ms. Clara Jenkins, a 32-year-old woman referred for an opinion regarding persistent mineral laboratory anomalies noted on routine screening.

Her baseline panel recently revealed an elevated serum inorganic phosphorus level, which persisted on repeat testing at 5.5 mg/dL. Her circulating calcium concentrations are completely normal, with both total and ionized fractions falling comfortably inside the expected reference range. In addition, her intact parathyroid hormone measurement was strictly unremarkable, displaying neither an abnormally high reading nor any decrease or suppression.

Ms. Jenkins reports feeling entirely well with no specific complaints. Her medical history is negative for major illnesses, and she takes no prescription medications. She works as an accountant and does not use tobacco or alcohol. Her physical examination was entirely unremarkable, demonstrating normal blood pressure, clear breath sounds, and no focal skeletal or neuromuscular signs. Renal indices, including serum blood urea nitrogen and creatinine, are well within normal limits.

In the context of sustained elevated phosphate alongside normal calcium and parathyroid hormone levels, I would be grateful for your clinical assessment and any recommendations for further workup.

Sincerely,

Dr. Arthur Miller
